techniques.name: Evaluator-Optimizer
techniques.description: Generate a candidate, evaluate it against explicit criteria, revise the highest-impact defect and repeat within a fixed budget.
techniques.purpose: Improve an output through targeted feedback rather than untracked rewriting.
techniques.problem_solved: Outputs are accepted after one pass or revised repeatedly without measurable convergence.
when_to_use: A draft has clear quality criteria and addressable defects
Evaluation can produce actionable, evidence-linked feedback
when_not_to_use: No reliable rubric exists
The task requires factual verification rather than stylistic optimization
trigger_conditions: A candidate fails one or more stated criteria
A bounded number of revision rounds is authorized
workflow_steps: Freeze the candidate version and rubric
Evaluate each criterion with cited defects
Select the smallest revision that addresses the highest-impact defect
Re-evaluate the revised version against the same rubric
Stop on acceptance, no improvement or the round limit
techniques.example_prompt: Evaluate this candidate against the fixed rubric, revise only the highest-impact defect and repeat within the declared round limit. Preserve each version and evaluation result.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: improve a draft's structure and citation completeness without allowing the optimizer to invent missing evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Each revision maps to a cited evaluation finding
The loop stops on acceptance, no improvement or the fixed limit
verification_procedure: Compare version history with the rubric results
Confirm unsupported claims were rejected rather than optimized away
security_considerations: Optimization must not remove safety, approval or provenance constraints
Evaluator feedback is not factual proof
techniques.fallback_procedure: Return the best version with unresolved criteria and request human editing instead of continuing unbounded optimization.

techniques.name: Reflection
techniques.description: Review an executed trace against intent and evidence to identify failure patterns and a bounded corrective action.
techniques.purpose: Turn completed work into explicit learning without rewriting history or claiming unsupported success.
techniques.problem_solved: Agents repeat mistakes because post-run review is absent, vague or detached from evidence.
when_to_use: A task, experiment or verification run has completed
A failure or near miss needs a durable lesson
when_not_to_use: No execution trace exists
Reflection would delay an urgent stop or escalation
trigger_conditions: A run ends with failure, surprise or a checkpoint
A repeated failure pattern is suspected
workflow_steps: Restate the intended outcome and actual observed outcome
Identify the first divergent decision or missing check
Classify the failure as evidence, planning, tool, permission or scope related
Propose one bounded corrective action with an owner
Record the lesson separately from any unverified root-cause claim
techniques.example_prompt: Reflect on this completed trace against the original intent. Cite the first divergence, distinguish observed facts from hypotheses and propose one bounded corrective action.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: review why a future digest validation draft omitted an effective-date check without claiming the product pipeline exists.
acceptance_criteria: Reflection cites exact trace evidence
Corrective actions are bounded and do not rewrite the execution record
verification_procedure: Compare the reflection with raw outcomes and acceptance criteria
Check that hypotheses are labeled and assigned validation steps
security_considerations: Do not copy secrets into reflection notes
Self-critique does not replace independent review for high-risk work
techniques.fallback_procedure: Write a short observed-facts and next-action note when a full reflection cannot be completed.

techniques.name: Cost-aware Model Routing and Cascading
techniques.description: Route tasks to the least-cost approved model tier that meets evidence-based quality and policy requirements, escalating only on defined signals.
techniques.purpose: Control model spend and latency without silently lowering quality or bypassing data policy.
techniques.problem_solved: Every request uses an expensive model or weak models fail silently on tasks that need stronger reasoning.
when_to_use: Multiple approved model tiers exist
Fixed evaluations can justify routing thresholds
when_not_to_use: No approved alternatives or evaluation baseline exists
Data policy permits only one provider or model
trigger_conditions: Task classes have different complexity or risk
A cheaper tier can be evaluated against a stable rubric
workflow_steps: Classify task complexity, risk and data-handling needs
Filter to policy-approved models before considering cost
Select the cheapest tier with sufficient evaluation evidence
Escalate only on explicit validation, confidence or rubric signals
Record the route, versions, reported usage and final quality result
techniques.example_prompt: Route this task through approved model tiers using evidence-based thresholds. Escalate only on the declared signals and do not claim savings or quality without recorded results.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: evaluate cheaper routing for routine draft formatting while keeping claim verification on an approved stronger tier; no provider call is authorized here.
acceptance_criteria: Policy filtering precedes cost selection
Every escalation has a recorded signal and outcome
verification_procedure: Run the fixed task set through each approved route
Compare quality, failures and provider-reported usage against the baseline
security_considerations: Never route restricted data to a cheaper but disallowed provider
Model confidence alone is not an escalation or acceptance guarantee
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use the single approved baseline model and mark routing benefits unknown until comparative evidence exists.

techniques.name: Ensemble Verification
techniques.description: Use multiple independent verification methods or perspectives and reconcile disagreements with evidence.
techniques.purpose: Reduce single-reviewer blind spots without treating agreement as proof.
techniques.problem_solved: One reviewer or checker misses defects that a different method or context would expose.
when_to_use: High-impact claims need independent checks
Different verifiers can test distinct properties or failure modes
when_not_to_use: Verifiers share the same hidden context or tool failure
A deterministic check fully covers the acceptance criterion
trigger_conditions: A claim is consequential or disputed
A single verification method has known blind spots
workflow_steps: Assign distinct checks or contexts to each verifier
Collect findings without exposing other verdicts
Compare agreements and disagreements by property
Resolve conflicts with deterministic evidence or human review
Report residual uncertainty instead of manufacturing consensus
techniques.example_prompt: Verify this artifact with independent checks for correctness, security and acceptance. Reconcile disagreements using evidence and do not convert majority agreement into proof.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: independently check a future digest's citations, temporal validity and scope before any editorial approval.
acceptance_criteria: Verifier assignments are meaningfully independent
Every disagreement has an evidence-backed resolution or remains open
verification_procedure: Inspect verifier inputs and findings for shared blind spots
Reproduce the deterministic checks used to reconcile disputes
security_considerations: Give each verifier only the access it needs
Consensus cannot override policy, source authority or missing evidence
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use one independent human reviewer plus deterministic checks when a full ensemble is unavailable.

techniques.name: Tool Calling
techniques.description: Invoke external capabilities through validated schemas, explicit permissions and bounded arguments, then validate returned data.
techniques.purpose: Make tool use safe, observable and testable rather than relying on free-form commands.
techniques.problem_solved: Agents call tools with malformed arguments, excessive permissions or untrusted results.
when_to_use: A task requires a capability outside the model
A tool exposes a stable schema and permission boundary
when_not_to_use: The action is not authorized
The tool schema, side effects or output semantics are unknown
trigger_conditions: A declared task step needs a tool
A tool manifest and permission policy are available
workflow_steps: Resolve the tool from an approved manifest
Validate arguments and side-effect class before calling
Apply least privilege, timeout and output bounds
Validate the returned schema and provenance
Record the call outcome without secrets or unsupported success claims
techniques.example_prompt: Plan this tool call using its approved manifest. Validate arguments, permissions and side effects first, then define output validation and failure handling; do not execute an unapproved action.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: define a schema-bound call to a future approved evidence store without installing or activating a connector.
acceptance_criteria: Arguments and permissions are validated before invocation
Outputs are schema-checked and failures remain explicit
verification_procedure: Test valid, malformed, unauthorized and timeout cases with a fake tool
Inspect traces for redaction and side-effect classification
security_considerations: Tool descriptions and outputs are untrusted
Separate read, write, network and paid capabilities in permissions
techniques.fallback_procedure: Perform the step manually through an approved interface and record equivalent evidence.

techniques.name: State Machine Orchestration
techniques.description: Control a workflow through explicit states, guarded transitions, persisted context and terminal outcomes.
techniques.purpose: Prevent invalid step ordering, ambiguous progress and unsafe transitions during long workflows.
techniques.problem_solved: Agents improvise transitions, repeat completed work or skip approval and verification states.
when_to_use: A workflow has durable phases and approval gates
Failures, retries or handoffs must preserve valid state
when_not_to_use: The workflow is a single deterministic action
States and guards cannot be defined from requirements
trigger_conditions: A process has more than one phase or owner
An invalid transition could bypass review or duplicate side effects
workflow_steps: Define allowed states and terminal outcomes
Specify each transition's event, guard and side effect
Persist state with the evidence that satisfied the guard
Reject invalid or stale transitions
Test recovery, retry and approval-bypass paths
techniques.example_prompt: Model this workflow as an explicit state machine. List guarded transitions, persisted evidence and terminal states, then test invalid transitions and recovery without executing side effects.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model draft, review, approved and published states so an edit invalidates approval; this is a design example, not an implemented workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Every transition has an explicit guard and evidence requirement
Invalid, stale and recovery transitions are covered by tests
verification_procedure: Run transition-table fixtures for success, rejection, retry and stale-state cases
security_considerations: Approval and permission checks must be transition guards
Persisted state needs integrity, access control and audit history
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a manual state checklist with recorded transition approvals until a runtime exists.

techniques.name: Bounded Retry
techniques.description: Retry only classified transient failures under explicit attempt, delay, budget and stop rules.
techniques.purpose: Recover from temporary faults without loops, duplicated side effects or hidden cost.
techniques.problem_solved: Unbounded retries repeat deterministic failures or duplicate non-idempotent actions.
when_to_use: A failure is plausibly transient
The operation is idempotent or has a deduplication key
when_not_to_use: The failure is deterministic or unauthorized
The action cannot safely be repeated
trigger_conditions: A tool or service returns a retryable timeout or transient status
A retry policy and idempotency guarantee exist
workflow_steps: Classify the failure as transient, deterministic, policy or unknown
Confirm the operation is safe to repeat
Apply the attempt, delay and total-budget limits
Reuse the same idempotency key when required
Stop with a structured failure when the limit or non-retryable class is reached
techniques.example_prompt: Decide whether this failure may be retried. Cite the error class and idempotency guarantee, enforce the declared limits and stop immediately on deterministic or policy failures.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: bound retries for a future approved notification delivery using a deduplication key; no notification channel is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Only transient safe failures are retried
Attempt count, delay and total budget are enforced and logged
verification_procedure: Exercise transient, deterministic, unauthorized and repeated-timeout fixtures
Confirm non-idempotent actions are never retried
security_considerations: Retries must not bypass rate limits, approvals or access controls
Backoff must not amplify denial-of-service conditions
techniques.fallback_procedure: Stop after the first failure and request human diagnosis when retry safety is unknown.

techniques.name: Behaviour-Driven Development
techniques.description: Translate business behavior into concrete scenarios, automate those scenarios and implement only what makes them pass.
techniques.purpose: Keep implementation tied to shared, business-readable examples of required behavior.
techniques.problem_solved: Technical tests pass while stakeholders disagree about the actual business behavior.
when_to_use: Business rules have multiple examples or edge cases
Developers, testers and product owners need a shared specification
when_not_to_use: The change is purely mechanical
No stakeholder can confirm scenario meaning
trigger_conditions: Acceptance criteria contain ambiguous behavior
A rule change needs executable business examples
workflow_steps: Write one behavior as a concrete given-when-then scenario
Add boundary and failure examples with the domain reviewer
Automate the scenarios and confirm the expected failure
Implement the smallest behavior that satisfies them
Review scenario names and evidence against the requirement
techniques.example_prompt: Convert this business rule into concrete given-when-then scenarios, including one failure case. Automate them before implementation and keep the language reviewable by a domain owner.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: specify that an expired policy claim cannot enter an eligible digest set, using fixtures rather than a live source.
acceptance_criteria: Scenarios are business-readable and traceable to a requirement
At least one scenario fails before implementation and passes afterward
verification_procedure: Review scenarios with the domain owner
Run the scenario suite before and after the change
security_considerations: Use synthetic examples without personal or confidential data
Scenario approval does not authorize external publication
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a reviewed example table and manual checks until a scenario runner is available.

techniques.name: Domain-Driven Design
techniques.description: Model complex business behavior with a ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates and explicit domain rules.
techniques.purpose: Align code boundaries and terminology with the business domain rather than technical layers alone.
techniques.problem_solved: Ambiguous terminology and scattered rules cause inconsistent behavior across modules.
when_to_use: The domain has rich concepts, invariants or multiple subdomains
Business and code terminology repeatedly diverge
when_not_to_use: The application is a simple CRUD wrapper
Domain experts cannot validate the model
trigger_conditions: Business rules span several modules
The same term has different meanings in different contexts
workflow_steps: Extract domain terms and resolve context-specific meanings
Identify bounded contexts and their relationships
Define aggregates, entities, value objects and invariants
Map business rules to model objects and tests
Review the model with a domain owner before changing code boundaries
techniques.example_prompt: Model this business domain using a ubiquitous language and bounded contexts. Identify aggregates and invariants, and flag terms whose meaning still needs domain-owner confirmation.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: distinguish source, evidence, claim and event concepts in a proposed model without creating a product database.
acceptance_criteria: Domain terms have context-specific definitions
Every invariant has an owner and a planned verification
verification_procedure: Review the glossary and context map with a domain owner
Trace each invariant to examples and model tests
security_considerations: Domain models must encode authorization and data-classification boundaries
Avoid copying sensitive business records into model examples
techniques.fallback_procedure: Start with a glossary and invariant list, then introduce aggregates only where domain complexity justifies them.

techniques.name: SOLID Design Principles
techniques.description: Review object and module boundaries against single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion.
techniques.purpose: Improve changeability and testability without applying principles as automatic abstraction rules.
techniques.problem_solved: Classes accumulate unrelated reasons to change or depend on concrete implementations and oversized interfaces.
when_to_use: Designing or reviewing classes, services and module contracts
A change repeatedly forces edits across unrelated responsibilities
when_not_to_use: The code is simple and the abstraction cost exceeds the benefit
No concrete changeability problem has been observed
trigger_conditions: A class or interface has multiple unrelated change drivers
Tests require concrete infrastructure or broad mock interfaces
workflow_steps: List each class or module responsibility and reason to change
Check substitutability and interface breadth at real call sites
Identify concrete dependencies that hinder isolated tests
Propose the smallest boundary change for a confirmed violation
Preserve behavior with characterization and regression tests
techniques.example_prompt: Review these boundaries against each SOLID principle using concrete call sites and change drivers. Recommend only the smallest justified refactor and reject speculative abstraction.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: review a proposed evidence-service boundary so storage details do not leak into claim-verification logic.
acceptance_criteria: Each finding cites a concrete responsibility, substitution or dependency problem
Refactoring preserves tested behavior and stays in scope
verification_procedure: Inspect before-and-after interfaces and call sites
Run characterization and regression tests for each boundary change
security_considerations: Abstraction must not hide authorization or validation
Do not broaden interfaces with sensitive operations for convenience
techniques.fallback_procedure: Keep the current boundary and record the design concern when no justified, behavior-preserving change is available.

techniques.name: Modular Monolith
techniques.description: Build one deployable application with enforced module boundaries, explicit contracts and independently testable internal concerns.
techniques.purpose: Gain modularity and team ownership without premature distributed-system complexity.
techniques.problem_solved: A codebase becomes a tangled monolith or is split into services before boundaries and operational needs are proven.
when_to_use: A new system needs clear modules but simple deployment
Domain boundaries are emerging and service extraction is not justified
when_not_to_use: Independent scaling, deployment or fault isolation is already required
Module boundaries cannot be enforced
trigger_conditions: Cross-module imports are increasing
A team is considering microservices without measured operational need
workflow_steps: Group capabilities by cohesive business responsibility
Define public module contracts and forbidden dependencies
Move shared code to an explicit owner or contract
Add architecture tests or review checks for boundary violations
Record extraction triggers instead of splitting services speculatively
techniques.example_prompt: Propose a modular-monolith boundary map for this system. Specify public contracts, forbidden dependencies and measurable triggers that would justify future service extraction.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: keep proposed evidence and digest modules in one deployable boundary until independent scaling is evidenced.
acceptance_criteria: Every module has a public contract and owner
Dependency rules are checked by tests or a documented review gate
verification_procedure: Run architecture dependency checks
Review cross-module call sites and shared-state ownership
security_considerations: Module boundaries must not bypass authorization
Shared databases require explicit schema and access ownership
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use package-level boundaries with manual dependency review until architecture tests exist.

techniques.name: Dependency Injection
techniques.description: Supply collaborators through explicit constructor or factory boundaries instead of constructing concrete dependencies inside business logic.
techniques.purpose: Make dependencies visible, replaceable and testable without hidden global state.
techniques.problem_solved: Business logic is tightly coupled to infrastructure and difficult to isolate in tests.
when_to_use: A component depends on external services, clocks, storage or configuration
Tests need controlled substitutes
when_not_to_use: A dependency is stable, internal and has no variability
Injection would only add indirection without a test or change need
trigger_conditions: Tests cannot run without live infrastructure
A class directly constructs or locates a collaborator
workflow_steps: Identify collaborators currently created or globally accessed
Define the narrow contract each consumer needs
Inject implementations at an explicit composition root
Test the consumer with controlled fakes
Review lifetimes, disposal and configuration for leaks or hidden state
techniques.example_prompt: Refactor these hidden concrete dependencies behind narrow injected contracts. Keep construction at one composition root and prove isolation with fake-based tests.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: inject a fake evidence repository into a future claim-verification component without provisioning a database.
acceptance_criteria: Business logic does not construct infrastructure collaborators
Consumer tests run with controlled substitutes and explicit lifetimes
verification_procedure: Inspect the composition root and dependency graph
Run tests with fakes and verify no live service is required
security_considerations: Do not inject credentials into domain objects or logs
Validate implementations at the composition boundary
techniques.fallback_procedure: Introduce a small factory seam first when full constructor injection would exceed the task scope.

techniques.name: Strategy Pattern
techniques.description: Encapsulate interchangeable algorithms behind one stable contract selected by explicit configuration or context.
techniques.purpose: Replace conditional algorithm branches with independently testable implementations.
techniques.problem_solved: Growing if/else or switch blocks mix policy selection with algorithm details.
when_to_use: Multiple algorithms satisfy the same contract
Selection varies by source, policy, task or configuration
when_not_to_use: Only one algorithm exists
Variation is speculative or the contract would be unstable
trigger_conditions: A conditional branch selects among processing algorithms
A new algorithm requires edits across unrelated call sites
workflow_steps: Extract the common algorithm contract from real branches
Move each branch into a named strategy
Define deterministic selection and default behavior
Test each strategy against shared contract cases
Add a selection test for unknown and disallowed identifiers
techniques.example_prompt: Replace these algorithm branches with explicit strategies behind one contract. Preserve behavior, test each strategy and define safe handling for unknown selections.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: select an approved date-normalization strategy by source format without embedding source-specific conditionals in the domain rule.
acceptance_criteria: Strategies share one tested contract
Selection is deterministic and unknown values fail safely
verification_procedure: Run shared contract cases for every strategy
Compare pre-refactor and post-refactor outputs for representative inputs
security_considerations: Strategy identifiers must not allow arbitrary class loading
Each strategy needs the same validation and authorization expectations
techniques.fallback_procedure: Keep the existing branch and add contract tests until a second real algorithm justifies extraction.

techniques.name: Repository Pattern
techniques.description: Expose persistence operations through a domain-oriented contract while keeping queries, mappings and transactions in an infrastructure implementation.
techniques.purpose: Decouple business rules from database APIs and make data access replaceable and testable.
techniques.problem_solved: Storage details and queries spread through business logic, causing brittle tests and duplicated persistence rules.
when_to_use: Domain logic depends on durable aggregates or evidence records
Multiple storage implementations or isolated tests are needed
when_not_to_use: The operation is a trivial direct query with no domain behavior
The abstraction would merely rename the database API
trigger_conditions: Business services construct storage calls directly
Data-access concerns hinder isolated domain tests
prerequisites: Fake or disposable storage for tests
workflow_steps: Define persistence needs in domain terms
Specify query, unit-of-work and failure semantics
Implement storage mapping behind the contract
Test the domain with an in-memory or disposable fake
Run integration tests for constraints, transactions and authorization
techniques.example_prompt: Define a repository contract for this aggregate without leaking database types. Specify transaction and query semantics, then test both a fake and an approved disposable store.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: isolate a proposed evidence-record repository from a future database choice; no database is created.
acceptance_criteria: Domain code has no storage API dependency
Transaction, query and authorization behavior has contract or integration evidence
verification_procedure: Run domain tests with a fake
Run approved integration fixtures for constraints, rollback and access control
security_considerations: Repository methods must enforce or delegate tenant and role authorization
Avoid generic APIs that expose unrestricted queries or sensitive fields
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a narrow data-access function with domain-language naming until a full repository is justified.

techniques.name: Pipeline Pattern
techniques.description: Compose ordered processing stages with explicit input/output contracts, validation, failure handling and observability.
techniques.purpose: Make multi-stage transformations reusable, testable and easy to diagnose.
techniques.problem_solved: Processing logic becomes one opaque function with hidden ordering, mutation and error behavior.
when_to_use: Data passes through repeated transform, validate or enrich stages
Stages need independent tests or replacement
when_not_to_use: The workflow is a single operation
Stages share so much implicit state that contracts would be artificial
trigger_conditions: A function mixes parsing, validation, transformation and output formatting
Failures cannot be attributed to a processing stage
workflow_steps: Define the envelope and provenance carried between stages
Implement one responsibility per stage with schema validation
Specify whether failures stop, skip or quarantine the record
Test each stage and one end-to-end fixture
Record stage versions, timings when measured and failure location
techniques.example_prompt: Refactor this processing flow into a staged pipeline. Define envelope contracts, validation and failure policy for each stage, then test stages independently and end to end.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model collect, normalize, extract and verify as separate future stages without enabling collection or model calls.
acceptance_criteria: Every stage has a validated input and output contract
A failing fixture identifies the exact stage and preserves provenance
verification_procedure: Run per-stage unit fixtures and an end-to-end fixture
Inject malformed input at each boundary and inspect failure records
security_considerations: Validate untrusted data at every trust boundary
Do not allow later stages to erase provenance or bypass authorization
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a linear script with explicit checkpoints until reusable stage contracts are proven.

techniques.name: Event-Driven Architecture
techniques.description: Coordinate producers, event contracts, brokers and consumers with explicit ordering, delivery and failure semantics.
techniques.purpose: Decouple asynchronous work while making event ownership and delivery guarantees explicit.
techniques.problem_solved: Direct calls couple workflows tightly or events are published without schemas, ordering and replay rules.
when_to_use: Independent consumers react to durable state changes
Asynchronous decoupling or replay is a real requirement
when_not_to_use: A synchronous request/response contract is sufficient
Operational complexity cannot be supported
trigger_conditions: Multiple consumers need the same state-change notification
Temporal coupling blocks independent operation
workflow_steps: Define event meaning, owner and schema version
Map producers, consumers and allowed dependencies
Specify ordering, duplication, retry and dead-letter behavior
Make consumers idempotent and test replay
Document retention, access and operational recovery
techniques.example_prompt: Design this event flow with versioned schemas and explicit delivery semantics. Make consumers idempotent, test duplicate and out-of-order events and document replay ownership.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: a future evidence-approved event could trigger draft regeneration; no broker, consumer or publication is implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Every event has an owner, version and consumer contract
Duplicate, out-of-order and replay cases have defined behavior and tests
verification_procedure: Run contract tests against a fake broker
Exercise duplicate, reordered, failed and replayed event fixtures
security_considerations: Events must not carry secrets or unauthorized tenant data
Consumers need authorization, replay limits and tamper-evident provenance
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a durable job table or explicit synchronous calls until broker operations are justified.

techniques.name: Feature Flags
techniques.description: Gate incomplete or risky behavior behind named, owned runtime flags with safe defaults and removal criteria.
techniques.purpose: Separate deployment from exposure and provide a controlled rollback path.
techniques.problem_solved: Unfinished features become visible on merge or rollback requires a code revert.
when_to_use: A feature needs staged exposure or independent rollout
A reversible kill switch reduces operational risk
when_not_to_use: The change is fully approved and needs no staged exposure
A flag would permanently hide an authorization or correctness rule
trigger_conditions: Code will merge before full user exposure is approved
A high-impact behavior needs a tested disable path
prerequisites: Test matrix for enabled and disabled states
workflow_steps: Name the flag, owner, purpose and safe default
Define targeting and approval rules
Test both flag states and transitions
Record audit events for changes and verify the disable path
Set an expiry or removal criterion
techniques.example_prompt: Design a feature flag for this staged change. Specify owner, safe default, targeting, tests for both states, audit events and a removal criterion.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: expose a future digest format to internal review before any public release; no UI or flag service exists.
acceptance_criteria: Both flag states and the disable path are tested
Every flag has an owner, safe default and removal criterion
verification_procedure: Run enabled, disabled and transition-state tests
Inspect flag-change audit records and rollback behavior
security_considerations: Flags must not bypass authorization or consent
Protect flag administration and audit every target change
techniques.fallback_procedure: Keep the feature unmerged or disabled in approved configuration until a controlled exposure mechanism exists.

techniques.name: Unit Testing
techniques.description: Test one isolated behavior or domain rule with controlled dependencies, deterministic fixtures and explicit assertions.
techniques.purpose: Localize defects quickly and document fine-grained behavior without infrastructure noise.
techniques.problem_solved: Bugs are discovered late in slow integrated flows or units lack precise behavioral coverage.
when_to_use: Implementing functions, classes or domain rules
A defect can be reproduced at a small boundary
when_not_to_use: The behavior only exists across external infrastructure
A test would assert private implementation details rather than behavior
trigger_conditions: A new or changed deterministic behavior exists
A bug has a minimal local reproduction
workflow_steps: Choose one observable behavior and its boundary
Build the smallest deterministic fixture
Assert result, error and relevant side effects
Run the test before and after the change
Review the test for implementation coupling and hidden network access
techniques.example_prompt: Add focused unit tests for this behavior using controlled fixtures. Cover one normal case and one boundary or failure case without relying on live services.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: unit-test whether an expired claim is eligible for a future digest using synthetic dates.
acceptance_criteria: Tests are deterministic and isolated from external services
Assertions cover expected results and meaningful failures
verification_procedure: Run the targeted unit suite and inspect failure output
Repeat the tests to detect order dependence or hidden shared state
security_considerations: Use synthetic data and no real secrets
Avoid tests that require production credentials or unrestricted network access
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a small manual assertion script with recorded inputs and outputs if the standard runner is unavailable.

techniques.name: Integration Testing
techniques.description: Verify interactions between real or realistic components, including contracts, persistence, transactions and failure propagation.
techniques.purpose: Detect defects that isolated unit tests cannot expose at module or infrastructure boundaries.
techniques.problem_solved: Components pass alone but fail when schemas, transactions, configuration or external services interact.
when_to_use: A change crosses module, database, queue or API boundaries
Contract compatibility and transaction behavior matter
when_not_to_use: No integration boundary exists
A live production system would be mutated
trigger_conditions: Two or more components must cooperate
A unit test uses fakes for the boundary under review
workflow_steps: Identify the exact boundary and contract under test
Start only approved disposable dependencies
Seed minimal fixtures and exercise success plus failure paths
Assert persistence, transaction and error propagation behavior
Clean up state and record environment and component versions
techniques.example_prompt: Design integration tests for this component boundary. Use disposable dependencies, verify success and rollback paths and record the exact environment versions.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: verify a proposed repository and schema together on a disposable fixture without creating a production evidence store.
acceptance_criteria: The real boundary is exercised in an isolated environment
Success, failure and cleanup behavior are asserted
verification_procedure: Run the integration suite twice and compare state cleanup
Inspect dependency versions and logs for hidden external calls
security_considerations: Never point integration tests at production data
Use least-privilege test credentials and synthetic records
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use contract tests plus a controlled fake and mark full integration verification as incomplete.

techniques.name: Regression Testing
techniques.description: Select and run tests that demonstrate previously working behavior remains unchanged after a modification.
techniques.purpose: Detect unintended side effects before integration or release.
techniques.problem_solved: A fix or refactor silently breaks unrelated behavior outside the new test.
when_to_use: Every behavior change, bug fix or structural refactor
A prior defect needs a permanent guard
when_not_to_use: No baseline behavior or test suite exists
A test is flaky or unrelated and cannot be interpreted
trigger_conditions: A diff changes shared code, contracts or data
A previously observed defect is fixed
workflow_steps: Map changed files and contracts to affected behavior
Select existing and new regression cases
Run the targeted set before broader checks
Compare failures with the known-good baseline
Record unrun or flaky checks as unresolved evidence gaps
techniques.example_prompt: Select regression tests for this diff based on changed behavior and shared dependencies. Report exact results and do not treat skipped or flaky checks as passing.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: rerun citation and date-validation fixtures after a proposed digest-rule change.
acceptance_criteria: Each material changed behavior has a regression check
Unrun, skipped and flaky checks are explicit
verification_procedure: Compare selected tests with the change-impact map
Inspect command output, exit codes and baseline results
security_considerations: Security-sensitive changes require dedicated security regression cases
Do not weaken assertions to make the suite green
techniques.fallback_procedure: Run the full deterministic suite and manually check untested behavior when selection is uncertain.

techniques.name: Property-Based Testing
techniques.description: State invariants and generate varied inputs to test whether those properties hold across a defined domain.
techniques.purpose: Find edge cases that hand-written examples miss while focusing tests on durable behavior.
techniques.problem_solved: Tests cover a few examples but fail on unusual valid or boundary inputs.
when_to_use: Inputs have many valid variations
A function has clear invariants such as round-trip, ordering or idempotence
when_not_to_use: The property cannot be stated precisely
Generated cases are too expensive or nondeterministic to interpret
trigger_conditions: Repeated boundary bugs appear
A parser, normalizer or validator accepts a broad input domain
workflow_steps: Write invariants in terms of observable behavior
Define valid generators and explicit domain constraints
Run with a recorded seed and case budget
Shrink each counterexample to a minimal failing input
Add the minimized case as a conventional regression test
techniques.example_prompt: Define properties for this function and generate varied valid inputs. Record the seed, shrink failures to minimal counterexamples and convert them into fixed regression cases.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: test that a future date parser preserves the original instant across supported formats and rejects invalid dates.
acceptance_criteria: Properties are precise and independent of implementation details
Counterexamples are minimized, reproducible and retained
verification_procedure: Replay failures with recorded seeds
Review generators for invalid, biased or out-of-domain cases
security_considerations: Generated inputs must not create unsafe file, network or command paths
Bound case counts and input sizes to avoid resource exhaustion
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a curated boundary-case table when no property-testing library is available.

techniques.name: Mutation Testing
techniques.description: Introduce small, controlled source mutations and check whether the existing test suite detects each one.
techniques.purpose: Measure test sensitivity to realistic defects rather than relying only on coverage percentages.
techniques.problem_solved: Tests execute many lines but would still pass when important logic is changed or removed.
when_to_use: Critical logic has weak or suspicious tests
Coverage is high but defect escape remains a concern
when_not_to_use: The suite is too slow for bounded mutation runs
Generated mutants cannot be mapped to meaningful behavior
trigger_conditions: A test suite reports high coverage without strong assertions
A defect escaped despite related tests
workflow_steps: Confirm the baseline suite passes
Select a bounded set of meaningful mutation operators
Apply one mutation at a time and run targeted tests
Classify killed, survived, timeout and equivalent mutants
Add tests only for survived mutants that represent observable behavior gaps
techniques.example_prompt: Run a bounded mutation analysis on this critical logic. Preserve the baseline, classify every mutant and propose tests only for meaningful surviving behavior gaps.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: mutate a proposed eligibility comparison to see whether future digest tests detect an off-by-one date error.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline tests pass before mutation
Every mutant is classified and meaningful survivors have a test action
verification_procedure: Replay selected killed and survived mutants
Review equivalent-mutant decisions and mutation scope
security_considerations: Mutation runs must use disposable copies
Do not mutate production code, credentials or security controls in place
techniques.fallback_procedure: Perform manual fault injection on a disposable copy and record the test response without claiming a mutation score.

techniques.name: Differential Testing
techniques.description: Run equivalent inputs through two implementations or versions and compare normalized outputs and side effects.
techniques.purpose: Detect behavioral divergence during migrations, replacements or performance-oriented rewrites.
techniques.problem_solved: A new implementation appears correct on examples but differs subtly from a trusted baseline.
when_to_use: Replacing a parser, algorithm, service or storage layer
Two versions must remain behaviorally compatible
when_not_to_use: The baseline is known to be incorrect without a documented exception
Outputs cannot be normalized meaningfully
trigger_conditions: A parallel implementation or migration is proposed
Unexpected output differences appear between versions
workflow_steps: Freeze the baseline and candidate versions
Define which output and side-effect differences matter
Run the same bounded fixture corpus through both
Normalize irrelevant formatting and classify each divergence
Resolve intended differences through requirements or fix unintended ones
techniques.example_prompt: Compare this candidate with the frozen baseline on the shared fixture corpus. Normalize only irrelevant differences and classify every remaining divergence as intended or defective.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: compare old and proposed evidence-normalization rules on synthetic records before a future migration.
acceptance_criteria: Both versions receive identical inputs and environment constraints
Every meaningful divergence is classified with evidence
verification_procedure: Replay reported differences and inspect raw outputs
Check that normalization did not hide semantic or security differences
security_considerations: Use synthetic or approved data for both implementations
Do not route restricted data to an unapproved comparison service
techniques.fallback_procedure: Compare a curated fixture table manually and record unresolved equivalence rules.

techniques.name: Snapshot Testing
techniques.description: Capture a reviewed serialized output baseline and fail on later changes until a human approves the new snapshot.
techniques.purpose: Expose unexpected output changes in stable, inspectable artifacts.
techniques.problem_solved: Rendered documents, schemas or diagrams change without anyone noticing small but important differences.
when_to_use: Output is deterministic and human-reviewable
Small serialization or rendering changes matter
when_not_to_use: Output contains volatile timestamps or random identifiers without normalization
Reviewers would approve snapshots without inspecting them
trigger_conditions: A generator or renderer produces stable structured output
A prior snapshot diff is unexplained
workflow_steps: Normalize approved volatile fields
Review and store the initial snapshot
Generate the candidate output
Inspect the exact diff and classify intended changes
Update the baseline only with explicit review evidence
techniques.example_prompt: Compare this generated output with its reviewed snapshot. Normalize only declared volatile fields, show the exact diff and require review before updating the baseline.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: snapshot a generated diagram description or digest schema while excluding run-specific timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshots are deterministic after declared normalization
Every baseline update has review evidence and a classified diff
verification_procedure: Regenerate output twice and compare stability
Inspect snapshot diffs for hidden semantic changes
security_considerations: Do not store secrets or personal data in snapshots
Treat generated snapshot content as untrusted until reviewed
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a reviewed golden output file and manual diff when no snapshot framework exists.

techniques.name: Red Teaming
techniques.description: Probe an AI or security-sensitive system with authorized adversarial cases to discover failure modes and control gaps.
techniques.purpose: Expose weaknesses that normal acceptance tests and threat models may miss.
techniques.problem_solved: Prompt injection, data leakage, unsafe tool use or policy bypasses remain hidden until adversarial testing.
when_to_use: A system handles untrusted input, model output or privileged tools
A security boundary needs empirical challenge
when_not_to_use: The target or attack scope is not authorized
Testing could affect production, third parties or real users
trigger_conditions: A new AI workflow or trust boundary is proposed
A high-risk control lacks adversarial evidence
prerequisites: Written authorization and rules of engagement
Safe test data and stop conditions
workflow_steps: Confirm authorized scope, target and stop conditions
Derive attack cases from threat hypotheses and trust boundaries
Run cases in isolation with synthetic data
Record reproducible control failures without exploiting unrelated systems
Assign remediation, retest and residual-risk decisions
techniques.example_prompt: Design an authorized red-team test plan for these declared threats. Use isolated synthetic targets, define stop conditions and record reproducible findings without claiming exploitation beyond scope.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: test whether malicious article text can influence a future evidence workflow or trigger an unapproved tool call.
acceptance_criteria: Every test maps to an authorized threat hypothesis
Findings include reproduction, impact, control gap and retest criteria
verification_procedure: Replay findings in the isolated environment
Security reviewer checks scope compliance and remediation evidence
security_considerations: No testing against unauthorized or production targets
Protect sensitive findings and avoid storing live secrets in fixtures
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use static abuse-case review and mark empirical red-team verification blocked until authorization exists.

techniques.name: Failure Injection
techniques.description: Introduce controlled dependency failures in an isolated environment and verify detection, retry bounds, recovery and data integrity.
techniques.purpose: Demonstrate resilience behavior under faults instead of assuming it from design.
techniques.problem_solved: Timeout, partial failure and dependency outage paths are untested and fail unpredictably.
when_to_use: A workflow depends on external services or durable state
Recovery and retry behavior are acceptance requirements
when_not_to_use: Injection would affect production or shared infrastructure
The failure mode cannot be safely isolated
trigger_conditions: A retry, fallback or recovery claim needs evidence
A dependency has known timeout or partial-write failure modes
workflow_steps: Define one fault and the expected system response
Inject it only in an isolated dependency
Observe timeout, retry, fallback and alert behavior
Verify recovery and durable-state integrity
Remove the fault and confirm the system returns to baseline
techniques.example_prompt: Inject this declared dependency fault in an isolated test environment. Verify detection, bounded retry, recovery and data integrity, then restore the baseline.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: simulate a future evidence-store timeout during draft generation without touching any live store.
acceptance_criteria: The injected fault is isolated and reversible
Detection, retry limits, recovery and integrity are asserted
verification_procedure: Replay the fault and inspect timing, retry count, recovery and state comparisons
security_considerations: Never inject faults into production or shared systems
Use synthetic data and ensure fault controls cannot escape the test boundary
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use fake dependencies that return scripted failures and mark real infrastructure resilience as unverified.

techniques.name: Acceptance Test Automation
techniques.description: Convert approved acceptance criteria into repeatable, traceable checks with explicit pass, fail and not-run states.
techniques.purpose: Make stakeholder acceptance reproducible and tied to exact requirements.
techniques.problem_solved: Acceptance depends on memory or manual spot checks and cannot be rerun consistently.
when_to_use: A feature has approved acceptance criteria
A release or task needs repeatable acceptance evidence
when_not_to_use: Criteria are ambiguous or unapproved
The test would require unauthorized production actions
trigger_conditions: A task moves toward completion or release
Acceptance criteria are stable enough to automate
workflow_steps: Assign stable IDs to approved acceptance criteria
Map each criterion to an observable test and fixture
Automate the check with explicit pass and fail conditions
Run in an approved environment and retain exact evidence
Block completion on failure or missing required results
techniques.example_prompt: Automate these approved acceptance criteria with traceable IDs and explicit outcomes. Do not infer a pass from skipped tests or unrelated evidence.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: verify that a future digest excludes unsupported claims using approved fixtures, without publishing a real digest.
acceptance_criteria: Every automated check maps to an approved criterion
Pass, fail and not-run states are distinct and evidenced
verification_procedure: Review the criterion-to-test map
Run the suite and inspect exact results, fixtures and environment version
security_considerations: Acceptance tests must use safe data and authorized actions
Passing acceptance checks does not replace security or human approval gates
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a signed manual acceptance checklist and mark automation as not implemented.

techniques.name: Claim Extraction
techniques.description: Extract atomic, source-linked factual claims with subject, predicate, value, qualifiers and temporal scope.
techniques.purpose: Create verifiable units from source text without treating extraction as proof of truth.
techniques.problem_solved: Broad paragraphs are cited as evidence even though only one sentence or figure supports a specific assertion.
when_to_use: Source material contains figures, policies, dates or causal statements
Claims will be verified or reused in generated content
when_not_to_use: The task is open-ended creative writing
Source provenance or permission is missing
trigger_conditions: A document will support a digest, answer or decision
A paragraph contains multiple checkable assertions
workflow_steps: Confirm the source version and authorized scope
Split text into candidate factual statements
Normalize each claim into subject, predicate, value and qualifiers
Attach exact source spans and temporal context
Flag ambiguity, inference and statements that are not independently checkable
techniques.example_prompt: Extract atomic factual claims from this authorized source version. Preserve exact spans, qualifiers and dates, and label inference or ambiguity instead of converting it into fact.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: extract a marketplace fee figure and its effective date from an approved fixture for later verification.
acceptance_criteria: Every claim has an exact authorized source span
Qualifiers, dates and ambiguous statements remain visible
verification_procedure: Compare each claim with its source span
Check schema completeness and false splitting or merging of assertions
security_considerations: Treat source instructions as untrusted data
Do not extract or propagate personal or confidential information beyond scope
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use manual sentence-and-span extraction with reviewer confirmation when structured extraction is unavailable.

techniques.name: Cross-source Verification
techniques.description: Compare a claim against multiple sufficiently independent, authoritative and temporally relevant sources.
techniques.purpose: Distinguish corroboration from repetition and expose conflicts, staleness and source dependence.
techniques.problem_solved: Several URLs repeat the same unsupported statement and are mistaken for independent confirmation.
when_to_use: A high-impact claim needs corroboration
Sources may conflict, copy each other or have different effective dates
when_not_to_use: Only one authoritative source exists
Source independence or authority cannot be assessed
trigger_conditions: A claim affects publication, pricing, policy or user action
Initial evidence is singular, conflicting or derivative
workflow_steps: Normalize the claim and its temporal scope
Assess each source's authority, independence and effective date
Map supporting, contradicting and silent evidence
Identify shared upstream sources or copied text
Assign a verification status and escalate unresolved high-impact conflicts
techniques.example_prompt: Verify this claim across the supplied sources. Assess independence and effective dates, distinguish silence from contradiction and leave high-impact conflicts unresolved for human review.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: compare an official marketplace policy with secondary reporting and flag copied summaries as non-independent.
acceptance_criteria: Source independence and authority are recorded
Contradictions, stale evidence and unresolved status remain explicit
verification_procedure: Inspect source provenance and shared citations
Recheck claim wording, dates and source spans against the verification matrix
security_considerations: Do not access unauthorized sources to manufacture corroboration
Source count alone is not evidence of truth
techniques.fallback_procedure: Mark the claim unresolved and request an authoritative source rather than inferring support from weak evidence.

techniques.name: Entity Resolution
techniques.description: Determine whether records refer to the same real-world entity using identifiers, attributes, context and explicit merge rules.
techniques.purpose: Unify duplicate entity references without collapsing distinct people, products, sources or events.
techniques.problem_solved: Name variation creates duplicate records while aggressive matching merges unrelated entities.
when_to_use: Records use inconsistent names, aliases or identifiers
Entity identity affects evidence, counting or personalization
when_not_to_use: No stable identity evidence exists
A false merge would create material harm
trigger_conditions: Duplicate entity candidates are detected
Cross-source records need a canonical identity link
workflow_steps: Normalize candidate identifiers and names without destroying originals
Compare stable identifiers, aliases and contextual attributes
Apply explicit match, non-match and review rules
Record evidence for every merge or split decision
Test ambiguous and adversarial near-match fixtures
techniques.example_prompt: Resolve whether these records represent the same entity. Preserve original identifiers, cite match evidence and route ambiguous near-matches to review instead of forcing a merge.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: link marketplace and policy-source records that refer to the same platform while keeping distinct regional entities separate.
acceptance_criteria: Every merge has evidence and a reversible decision record
Ambiguous and near-match cases are not automatically merged
verification_procedure: Review a labeled sample of matches and non-matches
security_considerations: Do not merge identities using sensitive attributes without authorization
Preserve provenance and provide correction or split procedures
techniques.fallback_procedure: Keep records separate with candidate links until a reviewer can resolve identity.

techniques.name: Event Clustering
techniques.description: Group source reports into real-world events using shared entities, time windows, locations and factual overlap while preserving distinct incidents.
techniques.purpose: Consolidate coverage of the same event without merging unrelated or repeated developments.
techniques.problem_solved: Duplicate news reports inflate event counts or separate reports fragment one developing story.
when_to_use: Multiple sources report related developments
Event-level evidence, counts or timelines are needed
when_not_to_use: Reports are too sparse to establish a shared event
Similar wording is the only available signal
trigger_conditions: Candidate reports share entities, dates or claims
A digest needs one event record with multiple sources
workflow_steps: Normalize report dates, entities and locations
Generate candidate groups using factual and temporal overlap
Distinguish the same event from recurring or related incidents
Preserve every member source and contradictory claim
Review borderline clusters and record split or merge decisions
techniques.example_prompt: Cluster these reports by real-world event, not wording alone. Preserve source links and contradictions, and flag recurring or related incidents that must remain separate.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: group several approved reports about one policy change while keeping a later reversal as a distinct event.
acceptance_criteria: Each cluster has an event rationale and complete member provenance
Related but distinct incidents remain separate
verification_procedure: Review boundary and recurring-event fixtures
Compare cluster membership with entity, date and claim evidence
security_considerations: Clustering must not amplify unverified claims
Avoid inferring sensitive identities or locations from weak matches
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a manually reviewed event timeline and leave uncertain reports unclustered.

techniques.name: Temporal Reasoning
techniques.description: Reason explicitly about publication, event, effective, expiry and observation times, including time zones and unknown dates.
techniques.purpose: Prevent current, historical and future claims from being treated as simultaneously valid.
techniques.problem_solved: Evidence is cited without accounting for when it was published, effective or superseded.
when_to_use: Policies, prices, schedules or events change over time
A claim's validity depends on an effective interval
when_not_to_use: The claim has no temporal dimension
Dates are unavailable and cannot be marked unknown
trigger_conditions: A source contains multiple date types
A digest or decision requires current-as-of reasoning
workflow_steps: Classify each date as publication, event, effective, expiry or observation time
Normalize time zones and preserve original date text
Compare intervals against the declared as-of time
Flag unknown, contradictory and superseded dates
Require revalidation when the reference time or source version changes
techniques.example_prompt: Analyze the temporal validity of these claims as of the stated time. Separate publication from effective dates, preserve unknowns and flag superseded or contradictory intervals.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: distinguish a policy announcement date from its effective date before a future seller digest uses the claim.
acceptance_criteria: Date types and time zones are explicit
Unknown and conflicting dates are not silently resolved
verification_procedure: Check boundary fixtures for start, end, expiry and time-zone changes
Recompute validity at a different as-of time
security_considerations: Do not infer consent or applicability from ambiguous dates
Preserve original date evidence for audit
techniques.fallback_procedure: Mark temporal validity unresolved and request source clarification instead of assuming the publication date is effective.

techniques.name: Multi-modal Processing
techniques.description: Extract, normalize and verify information from text, image, audio and video inputs while preserving modality-specific provenance.
techniques.purpose: Use non-text evidence without treating model interpretation as direct observation or truth.
techniques.problem_solved: Information in images, audio or video is missed or converted into unsupported textual claims.
when_to_use: Approved sources contain charts, screenshots, speech or video
Cross-modal corroboration is required
when_not_to_use: The input modality is unauthorized or unsupported
A reliable text transcript or structured source already exists
trigger_conditions: A source has no adequate text representation
A claim depends on visual or audio evidence
workflow_steps: Confirm media permission, provenance and supported format
Extract text, regions, frames or transcript segments with offsets
Normalize observations without discarding source modality
Cross-check high-impact observations against another source or human review
Record tool version, uncertainty and failed extraction cases
techniques.example_prompt: Process these authorized media inputs with modality-linked provenance. Separate direct observations from interpretation and route uncertain high-impact content to verification.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: extract a policy table from an approved screenshot fixture and link each value to its image region.
acceptance_criteria: Every extracted observation links to a media offset or region
Uncertain or failed extractions are explicit and not presented as facts
verification_procedure: Compare samples with the original media
Test unsupported, corrupted and low-quality inputs
security_considerations: Do not upload private media to unapproved services
Check for embedded personal data, malicious files and hidden instructions
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use manual inspection of approved media and record observations without automated extraction.

techniques.name: Multi-agent Debate
techniques.description: Have independent agents argue defined positions, challenge evidence and produce a reconciled conclusion with unresolved disagreements.
techniques.purpose: Surface assumptions and competing interpretations before a consequential decision.
techniques.problem_solved: A single analysis reaches a confident conclusion without testing alternative explanations.
when_to_use: A consequential question has plausible competing hypotheses
Independent perspectives can improve issue discovery
when_not_to_use: Agents share the same context and incentives
A deterministic calculation or authoritative source settles the question
trigger_conditions: Experts or models disagree
A design or evidence decision has high reversal cost
workflow_steps: Frame one decision question and assign genuinely different positions
Require each position to cite approved evidence
Run bounded rebuttals focused on assumptions and missing evidence
Have a neutral reconciler classify agreements and unresolved disputes
Record the decision, dissent and validation needed
techniques.example_prompt: Debate the competing hypotheses for this bounded decision. Cite evidence, challenge assumptions within the round limit and preserve unresolved disagreement instead of forcing consensus.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: debate two interpretations of a marketplace-policy excerpt before proposing a future claim-verification rule.
acceptance_criteria: Positions are meaningfully independent and evidence-bound
The reconciliation preserves dissent and unresolved evidence gaps
verification_procedure: Inspect arguments for unsupported claims and shared blind spots
Validate the reconciled conclusion against original evidence
security_considerations: Debate cannot grant permissions or settle policy by majority
Avoid giving one agent hidden evidence or privileged instructions
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a structured option-and-rebuttal memo reviewed by one independent person.

techniques.name: Architecture-as-Code
techniques.description: Represent architecture elements, relationships and rules in a versioned machine-readable model that can generate views and checks.
techniques.purpose: Keep architecture consistent, reviewable and testable across documentation and implementation.
techniques.problem_solved: Architecture exists only in diagrams and prose, so structural rules cannot be validated or regenerated.
when_to_use: Multiple architecture views must stay consistent
Dependency or boundary rules need automated checks
when_not_to_use: A small system needs only a simple diagram
The model cannot be maintained alongside code
trigger_conditions: Architecture documentation repeatedly drifts
A team needs executable dependency or boundary rules
workflow_steps: Define model elements, relationships and stable identifiers
Encode architecture constraints separately from generated views
Generate the minimum views needed for review
Validate model syntax and architectural rules
Commit source, generated outputs and evidence with version parity
techniques.example_prompt: Model this architecture as versioned code with stable IDs and explicit dependency rules. Generate only the needed views and report validation separately from rendering.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: represent proposed Ecomdy module boundaries in a model while keeping DevHarness outside the product runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Model and generated views share one versioned source
Architecture constraints have machine or documented review checks
verification_procedure: Regenerate views and compare source parity
Run constraint fixtures for allowed and forbidden dependencies
security_considerations: Do not expose sensitive infrastructure details in generated public views
Treat generated files as derived artifacts, not independent authority
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a structured YAML or JSON inventory with manual view generation until a modeling tool is approved.

techniques.name: Architecture Drift Detection
techniques.description: Compare observed code, dependencies, deployment and data flows with the approved architecture model and classify differences.
techniques.purpose: Detect undocumented architectural change before it undermines assumptions or controls.
techniques.problem_solved: Documentation describes intended structure while the implemented system quietly violates it.
when_to_use: Architecture rules exist and implementation evolves
A review needs evidence of structural conformance
when_not_to_use: No approved architecture baseline exists
Observed state cannot be inspected safely
trigger_conditions: A dependency, module, deployment or data flow changes
Generated architecture checks report a mismatch
workflow_steps: Freeze the approved architecture version
Extract observed components, dependencies and interfaces
Compare structure using stable identifiers
Classify each difference as violation, intentional evolution or unknown
Assign remediation or an architecture-decision update with review
techniques.example_prompt: Compare observed dependencies and interfaces with this approved architecture model. Classify every difference and require review before changing either the code or the baseline.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: detect whether a proposed module begins depending directly on another module's storage implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Every reported difference cites observed and expected structure
Unknown differences are not silently accepted
verification_procedure: Reproduce extraction and compare stable IDs
Review false positives and intentional architecture decisions
security_considerations: Architecture scans must avoid secret-bearing files and private systems
Drift findings require review before automated remediation
techniques.fallback_procedure: Perform a manual dependency and documentation comparison and mark coverage limitations.

techniques.name: Data Flow Modeling
techniques.description: Model how data enters, moves, transforms, persists and leaves a system with sources, sinks, stores and trust boundaries.
techniques.purpose: Make data handling, ownership and security boundaries explicit before implementation.
techniques.problem_solved: Teams understand components but not where sensitive data travels or which process transforms it.
when_to_use: Designing data pipelines or integrations
Threat modeling, privacy review or provenance design
when_not_to_use: No data crosses a meaningful boundary
A simple sequence diagram communicates the same flow
trigger_conditions: A new source, store, processor or export is proposed
Data classification or retention is unclear
workflow_steps: Identify data elements and classification
Map sources, processors, stores and sinks
Annotate transformations, ownership and retention
Draw trust and permission boundaries
Validate the model against requirements and threat cases
techniques.example_prompt: Model this data flow from source to sink. Label classification, transformations, stores, retention and trust boundaries, and identify unapproved paths.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: map an approved source fixture through normalization and claim verification to a draft without enabling live collection.
acceptance_criteria: Every data path has a source, destination and owner
Trust, classification and retention boundaries are explicit
verification_procedure: Walk each path against actual contracts and fixtures
Security reviewer checks boundary crossings and unapproved sinks
security_considerations: Do not omit sensitive or failure paths from the model
External sinks require explicit data-handling approval
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a structured source-process-store-sink table if diagram tooling is unavailable.

techniques.name: Sequence Modeling
techniques.description: Model ordered interactions among actors and components, including alternatives, errors, timeouts and retries.
techniques.purpose: Clarify runtime behavior and handoffs that structural architecture views do not show.
techniques.problem_solved: Teams implement the right components in the wrong order or miss failure and timeout paths.
when_to_use: A workflow crosses multiple actors or services
Ordering, authorization or retry behavior is consequential
when_not_to_use: The interaction is a single synchronous call
A state model better represents the behavior
trigger_conditions: A new API or workflow is designed
A defect involves ordering, timeout or handoff
workflow_steps: Choose one use case and define participants
List ordered messages with preconditions and responses
Add timeout, error, retry and cancellation alternatives
Check authorization and idempotency at each call
Validate the model against contracts and test cases
techniques.example_prompt: Model this interaction sequence with success, timeout and retry alternatives. Show preconditions, responses and idempotency boundaries instead of only drawing the happy path.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model a future review request where an edited draft invalidates approval and requires a new review.
acceptance_criteria: Ordering and alternatives are explicit
Each call has a contract, failure behavior and relevant security check
verification_procedure: Trace the model against API contracts and fixtures
Review timeout, retry and cancellation paths with implementers
security_considerations: Do not expose secrets or tokens in sequence artifacts
Authorization checks must occur at the correct boundary
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a numbered interaction table with alternatives and failure handling.

techniques.name: ERD Modeling
techniques.description: Model entities, keys, relationships, cardinality, constraints and ownership for a persistent data design.
techniques.purpose: Make data structure and integrity rules reviewable before schema implementation or migration.
techniques.problem_solved: Schemas accumulate ambiguous relationships, duplicated facts and missing integrity constraints.
when_to_use: Designing or changing a persistent schema
Reviewing migration impact and data ownership
when_not_to_use: No durable relational data is involved
The schema is trivial and already fully specified
trigger_conditions: New entities or relationships are proposed
A migration changes keys, cardinality or constraints
workflow_steps: Define entities, stable keys and ownership
Specify relationships and cardinality from business rules
Add uniqueness, nullability and integrity constraints
Check normalization against actual query and update needs
Validate the model with migration and access-control fixtures
techniques.example_prompt: Create an ERD for this bounded data model. Specify keys, cardinality and integrity constraints, and identify ownership or normalization questions that need review before migration.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model source, evidence and claim relationships for a proposed store without creating a database.
acceptance_criteria: Every relationship has cardinality and ownership
Integrity constraints map to business rules and migration checks
verification_procedure: Review valid and invalid relationship fixtures
Compare the ERD with migration SQL or schema definitions
security_considerations: Classify sensitive attributes and minimize stored data
ERDs must not expose real records or credentials
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a table of entities, keys and relationships if a visual ERD cannot be rendered.

techniques.name: Design Tokens
techniques.description: Define shared semantic values for color, typography, spacing, motion and diagram styling with named usage rules.
techniques.purpose: Keep UI and visual documentation consistent without scattering raw design values.
techniques.problem_solved: Components and diagrams drift in styling and redesigns require broad manual edits.
when_to_use: A design system or multiple visual surfaces exist
Teams need consistent accessible and brand-approved styles
when_not_to_use: A single static artifact needs no reuse
Token semantics would be invented without design authority
trigger_conditions: Repeated raw values appear across components or diagrams
A visual redesign or accessibility correction needs coordinated change
workflow_steps: Inventory repeated visual values and their purposes
Define semantic token names rather than raw-value aliases
Specify allowed usage, fallback and deprecation behavior
Apply tokens to representative components or diagrams
Validate contrast, consistency and migration coverage
techniques.example_prompt: Create semantic design tokens for these repeated visual values. Include usage constraints and accessibility checks, and do not encode unapproved brand choices.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: align a future editorial dashboard and diagram palette through shared semantic tokens; no UI is implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens have semantic names and explicit usage rules
Representative visuals use tokens and pass contrast checks
verification_procedure: Search for remaining raw values in scoped assets
Compare rendered samples and accessibility results
security_considerations: Do not embed tenant data or secrets in token definitions
Review generated assets for unsafe external resources
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a small reviewed style constants file until a full token system is justified.

techniques.name: Screenshot-Driven Development
techniques.description: Translate an approved reference screenshot into explicit layout, content, state and responsive requirements before implementation.
techniques.purpose: Reduce visual guesswork while preserving accessibility and behavior beyond pixel imitation.
techniques.problem_solved: Developers infer spacing, states and responsive behavior from an image and miss design intent.
when_to_use: An approved visual reference exists
A UI change must match a reviewed design
when_not_to_use: The screenshot is unapproved, stale or contains sensitive data
No runnable UI or design specification exists
trigger_conditions: A design handoff consists mainly of screenshots
Visual parity needs a reviewable implementation target
workflow_steps: Confirm screenshot version, scope and viewport
Extract layout hierarchy, spacing, content and visible states
Identify missing responsive, loading, error and accessibility requirements
Implement the smallest component set against the specification
Compare in a browser and record intentional deviations
