techniques.example_prompt: Turn this approved screenshot into a layout and state specification. Identify missing responsive and accessibility behavior before implementing, then compare the result in a browser.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: implement a future digest-review mockup from an approved fixture without treating the screenshot as an approved product requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation traces to a versioned visual specification
Responsive, error and accessibility behavior is checked beyond pixel parity
verification_procedure: Compare scoped viewports in an approved browser
Review accessibility and intentional deviation records
security_considerations: Redact sensitive data in screenshots and traces
Do not fetch remote design assets without approval
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a written layout and state checklist when browser or screenshot tooling is unavailable.

techniques.name: Living Documentation
techniques.description: Update authoritative documentation in the same change as code, contracts or architecture, with ownership and freshness checks.
techniques.purpose: Keep documentation trustworthy and useful instead of allowing it to decay after implementation.
techniques.problem_solved: Documentation describes obsolete behavior and cannot be tied to the current version.
when_to_use: A change alters behavior, setup, APIs, architecture or operations
Documentation is part of the definition of done
when_not_to_use: No user or maintainer-facing behavior changed
A change is still an unapproved proposal
trigger_conditions: A PR changes code or contracts
A validation or review finds stale instructions
workflow_steps: Identify which authoritative documents the change affects
Update behavior, examples and limitations in the same task
Mark target design separately from observed as-built state
Run link, terminology and documentation validators
Assign an owner and review trigger for time-sensitive content
techniques.example_prompt: Update the authoritative documentation affected by this change. Preserve target-versus-as-built distinctions, validate links and record any content that still needs owner review.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: document a future citation-rule change alongside its tests while keeping proposed Ecomdy behavior clearly labeled.
acceptance_criteria: Every material behavior change has a documentation delta
Documentation distinguishes verified state from proposals and passes validation
verification_procedure: Compare the diff with documentation changes
Run validators and sample instructions against the current implementation
security_considerations: Do not publish secrets, private source text or unsupported capability claims
Generated documentation requires source and freshness checks
techniques.fallback_procedure: Add a bounded change note and owner follow-up when the authoritative document cannot be updated safely in the same task.

techniques.name: Short-lived Branches
techniques.description: Keep issue branches narrowly scoped, frequently synchronized and merged or closed within an explicit age limit.
techniques.purpose: Reduce merge debt, stale diffs and hidden long-running divergence.
techniques.problem_solved: Large or abandoned branches accumulate conflicts and bypass timely review.
when_to_use: Work is tracked by discrete issues or task contracts
Shared-branch integration is protected by review
when_not_to_use: A long-running release branch is explicitly required
The branch has no bounded objective or owner
trigger_conditions: A new issue enters implementation
A branch exceeds its age, size or synchronization threshold
workflow_steps: Create a branch from the approved current base with a task ID
Limit the diff to the task contract
Sync or rebase only through the approved safe procedure
Review age, size and conflict indicators
Merge, split or close the branch before limits are exceeded
techniques.example_prompt: Assess this issue branch against scope, age, size and base-branch freshness. Recommend merge, split, sync or closure without rewriting shared history.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: keep a technique-card update on a small issue branch and avoid unrelated registry changes.
acceptance_criteria: Branch maps to one bounded task
Age, size and freshness limits are checked before merge
verification_procedure: Inspect branch ancestry, diff and task mapping
Compare base and branch heads for stale or unrelated changes
security_considerations: Do not force-push shared branches or bypass review
Branch names and logs must not contain secrets
techniques.fallback_procedure: Keep work local and unmerged until it can be split into a reviewable branch.

techniques.name: Trunk-Based Development
techniques.description: Integrate small reviewed changes frequently into a shared trunk while using short branches or feature flags for incomplete exposure.
techniques.purpose: Minimize long-lived divergence and keep integration risk continuously visible.
techniques.problem_solved: Infrequent large merges hide conflicts, regressions and incomplete integration.
when_to_use: The team has reliable CI and review gates
Changes can be kept small and safely disabled until ready
when_not_to_use: CI or review is unreliable
A release train requires a separately approved long-lived branch
trigger_conditions: Integration delays or merge conflicts are increasing
A branch approaches the short-lived limit
workflow_steps: Split work into the smallest reviewable increments
Require passing checks and independent review before integration
Merge to trunk frequently within the approved cadence
Use controlled flags for incomplete user exposure
Monitor integration failures and rollback or pause when thresholds are exceeded
techniques.example_prompt: Assess this change for frequent trunk integration. Split oversized scope, require current checks and review, and use a controlled flag rather than a long-lived branch when exposure must be delayed.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: integrate small advisory harness changes frequently while keeping product features unimplemented.
acceptance_criteria: Integrated increments are small, reviewed and green
Incomplete exposure is controlled without bypassing trunk protections
verification_procedure: Inspect merge cadence, branch age and CI results
Review rollback and feature-flag evidence for incomplete work
security_considerations: Trunk-based development never authorizes direct pushes or skipped review
Protect required checks and avoid force-pushing shared history
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use short-lived branches with serialized merges until CI reliability supports frequent integration.

techniques.name: Scope Guard
techniques.description: Compare every proposed or observed change with the task's allowed paths, contracts and non-goals before accepting it.
techniques.purpose: Detect and stop scope expansion, unrelated cleanup and unauthorized file changes.
techniques.problem_solved: Agents modify convenient but out-of-scope files or hide extra changes inside a larger task.
when_to_use: Every mutating task
Reviewing generated patches or multi-agent output
when_not_to_use: No mutation is proposed
The task contract lacks an explicit scope
trigger_conditions: A diff or plan includes a new path or contract
A requested action exceeds declared non-goals
workflow_steps: Load the approved task scope and non-goals
List every changed or proposed path and contract
Classify each change as required, dependent or unrelated
Block unrelated changes and request approval for necessary expansion
Recheck scope after each execution or generation step
techniques.example_prompt: Check this diff against the approved task contract. Identify every out-of-scope path or contract change and stop unrelated edits rather than folding them into the task.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: prevent a technique-card data update from modifying the main technique registry or schema.
acceptance_criteria: Every changed path has a scope rationale
Unrelated changes are blocked or separately approved
verification_procedure: Compare Git diff and generated-file inventory with allowed paths
Review dependency-related exceptions with the task owner
security_considerations: Scope checks complement but do not replace filesystem permissions
Never treat an agent's own scope expansion as approval
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a manual changed-path checklist and stop when scope cannot be established.

techniques.name: Least Privilege
techniques.description: Grant each agent, tool, credential and runtime only the permissions required for the approved task and duration.
techniques.purpose: Limit the blast radius of mistakes, prompt injection and compromised components.
techniques.problem_solved: Broad credentials and tool permissions allow unrelated reads, writes, network access or paid actions.
when_to_use: Provisioning agents, tools, service accounts or CI runners
Reviewing permission changes
when_not_to_use: No privileged capability is needed
Permissions cannot be mapped to a task requirement
trigger_conditions: A new tool, connector or credential is proposed
A role requests broader access than its task requires
workflow_steps: List the exact actions and resources required by the task
Map each action to the narrowest role, tool and credential
Separate read, write, network, paid and administrative capabilities
Test allowed and denied actions with safe fixtures
Set expiry, rotation, revocation and periodic review
techniques.example_prompt: Derive a least-privilege permission matrix for this task. Deny capabilities that are not required and define expiry, rotation and revocation before access is granted.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: give a future evidence reviewer read-only access to approved records without publication or source-management rights.
acceptance_criteria: Every permission maps to a required action
Denied actions and credential lifecycle controls are tested and documented
verification_procedure: Run allowed and denied permission fixtures
Review credential scope, expiry and revocation evidence
security_considerations: Never share administrator credentials or place them in prompts
Local policy cannot replace host and cloud access controls
techniques.fallback_procedure: Deny the capability and use a human-mediated action until narrow access can be verified.

techniques.name: Pre-commit Hooks
techniques.description: Run fast, deterministic formatting, schema, secret and scope checks before a commit is created.
techniques.purpose: Catch local defects early while keeping commits reviewable and free of obvious policy violations.
techniques.problem_solved: Developers discover formatting, schema or secret issues only after push or CI.
when_to_use: Checks are fast, local and deterministic
The repository has an approved hook mechanism
when_not_to_use: A hook requires network, paid services or unbounded execution
The hook would silently modify unrelated files
trigger_conditions: A commit is about to be created
A repeated local defect should be prevented
workflow_steps: Inspect only staged content and declared checks
Run bounded local validators without network access
Report exact findings and leave unrelated files untouched
Block the commit on material failures
Verify hook version and any approved bypass record
techniques.example_prompt: Design pre-commit checks for this staged diff using fast local validators. Block on schema, secret or scope failures and do not modify unrelated files or require network access.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: run a future technique-schema check on staged catalogue data without changing the main registry.
acceptance_criteria: Hooks are deterministic, bounded and scoped to staged changes
Failures block the commit with exact findings
verification_procedure: Test clean, malformed, secret-bearing and over-limit staged fixtures
Inspect hook configuration and approved bypass records
security_considerations: Hooks are convenience controls and can be bypassed
Do not execute unreviewed hook code or log secrets
techniques.fallback_procedure: Run the same checks manually on staged content and record the results before committing.

techniques.name: Policy-as-Code
techniques.description: Express approved organizational or security rules as versioned, testable checks with explicit enforcement and exception handling.
techniques.purpose: Make policy consistent, reviewable and auditable across repositories and automation.
techniques.problem_solved: Rules live only in prose and are applied inconsistently or cannot be tested before enforcement.
when_to_use: A rule is stable, authoritative and machine-checkable
Multiple repositories or pipelines need consistent enforcement
when_not_to_use: The policy is ambiguous or still proposed
A check would encode an unapproved interpretation
trigger_conditions: A policy repeatedly causes review debate
A new CI, deployment or access rule is approved
workflow_steps: Translate one approved rule into a testable assertion
Define inputs, severity and enforcement point
Add compliant, violating and exception fixtures
Run checks in advisory mode before blocking
Version rule changes and audit every exception with an owner and expiry
techniques.example_prompt: Convert this approved policy into a testable rule. Define severity, enforcement and exception handling, and validate compliant and violating fixtures before enabling blocking behavior.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: encode a future requirement that published digest claims must cite authorized evidence, without claiming enforcement exists.
acceptance_criteria: Every rule traces to an approved policy source
Compliant, violating and expired-exception cases are tested
verification_procedure: Run policy fixtures and inspect enforcement logs
Review rule changes and exception records with the policy owner
security_considerations: Policy code is security-sensitive and requires review
Exceptions must be narrow, time-bound and auditable
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a reviewed manual policy checklist and record gaps until rules can be safely encoded.

techniques.name: Scheduled Automation
techniques.description: Run approved recurring jobs on an explicit schedule with idempotency, overlap prevention, budgets, logging and pause controls.
techniques.purpose: Automate periodic work without duplicate runs, silent drift or uncontrolled resource use.
techniques.problem_solved: Scheduled jobs overlap, retry indefinitely, use stale configuration or continue after failures.
when_to_use: A task has a genuine time-based cadence
The job is idempotent and has an operational owner
when_not_to_use: An event trigger is more appropriate
No approval, monitoring or pause mechanism exists
trigger_conditions: A recurring requirement has an approved cadence
A manual periodic task causes delays or omissions
workflow_steps: Confirm cadence, time zone and operational owner
Make the job idempotent and prevent overlapping runs
Apply source, runtime, cost and retry limits
Log run IDs, outcomes and freshness without secrets
Test pause, resume, missed-run and failure behavior
techniques.example_prompt: Design this recurring job with an explicit schedule, overlap lock and budget. Define idempotency, logging, alerting and pause behavior before enabling any automation.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: plan a future approved source-check schedule; no crawler or scheduler is activated.
acceptance_criteria: Schedule, owner and time zone are explicit
Overlap, retry, budget and pause behavior is tested
verification_procedure: Simulate on-time, overlapping, missed and failed runs
Inspect run logs, freshness and pause controls
security_considerations: Scheduled credentials need least privilege and rotation
No job may expand source access or publication authority automatically
techniques.fallback_procedure: Use a human-run checklist with recorded cadence until scheduling controls are approved.

techniques.name: Event-driven Automation
techniques.description: Trigger bounded automation from authenticated events with schema validation, deduplication, authorization and replay controls.
techniques.purpose: Respond to approved system events without trusting payloads or creating duplicate side effects.
techniques.problem_solved: Webhook or event handlers act on spoofed, malformed or duplicate events and repeat mutations.
when_to_use: An approved external or internal event should start a workflow
Event authenticity and idempotency can be verified
when_not_to_use: The event source is unauthenticated
A periodic schedule is the correct trigger
trigger_conditions: A supported event occurs
An event schema and authorization policy exist
workflow_steps: Authenticate the event source and validate the payload schema
Authorize the requested action against policy
Deduplicate using an event ID or idempotency key
Run the bounded workflow and record its outcome
Handle replay, ordering and malformed-event cases safely
techniques.example_prompt: Design an event-triggered automation contract. Authenticate and validate events, authorize actions, deduplicate side effects and define replay and malformed-event handling.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: a future approved review event could invalidate a digest approval; no Jira, GitHub or product event handler is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated, malformed and unauthorized events are rejected
Duplicate and replayed events do not duplicate side effects
verification_procedure: Exercise valid, spoofed, duplicate, reordered and malformed fixtures
Inspect authorization, deduplication and audit records
security_considerations: Event payloads are untrusted and may contain injection text
Verify signatures, replay windows and least-privilege actions
techniques.fallback_procedure: Queue the event for manual review when authenticity or idempotency cannot be established.

techniques.name: Budget Enforcement
techniques.description: Set and enforce hard limits for iterations, runtime, tokens, tool calls, network use and paid spend before and during execution.
techniques.purpose: Prevent runaway work, surprise cost and resource exhaustion with explicit stop behavior.
techniques.problem_solved: Tasks continue after their useful limit or exceed approved operational cost without a reliable stop.
when_to_use: Agent loops, batch jobs or paid services are used
A task has a declared resource ceiling
when_not_to_use: The action is a single bounded local operation
No reliable counter or stop mechanism exists
trigger_conditions: A task starts with resource limits
Observed usage approaches a configured threshold
workflow_steps: Define hard and warning limits for each resource
Choose counters that fail closed when usage is unknown
Check limits before each iteration or external call
Stop, checkpoint or escalate at the declared threshold
Record observed usage separately from estimates and unmeasured values
techniques.example_prompt: Enforce the declared task budgets before and during execution. Stop at hard limits, record observed usage and mark unknown token or cost values instead of estimating them as facts.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: cap a future batch evidence review by records and runtime without enabling paid model calls.
acceptance_criteria: Every hard limit has a tested stop action
Observed, estimated and unknown usage are clearly separated
verification_procedure: Test below-limit, warning, hard-limit and counter-failure fixtures
Inspect stop timing and checkpoint or escalation records
security_considerations: Budget controls must not be bypassable by retries or child jobs
Cost limits do not replace data or permission controls
techniques.fallback_procedure: Reduce task scope to one bounded step and stop if usage cannot be measured reliably.

techniques.name: Reproducible Environments
techniques.description: Define and verify toolchain, dependency, configuration and data setup so a clean environment produces equivalent results.
techniques.purpose: Remove hidden machine state and make setup, tests and evidence repeatable across developers and CI.
techniques.problem_solved: A task passes on one machine but fails elsewhere because of unpinned tools, implicit configuration or stale state.
when_to_use: Onboarding, CI or release preparation
Test failures may depend on local environment drift
when_not_to_use: The task has no executable environment
Reproduction would require copying secrets or private production data
trigger_conditions: A clean clone is set up
Results differ across machines or runners
workflow_steps: Inventory required runtimes, tools and dependencies
Pin versions, sources and configuration schemas
Create a clean environment without inherited user state
Run the declared setup and verification commands
Compare outputs and record platform-specific differences
techniques.example_prompt: Define a clean reproducible environment for this repository. Pin approved versions and sources, exclude secrets and verify setup from an empty workspace rather than relying on local caches.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: reproduce advisory harness validators in a clean container using only repository-declared dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Environment inputs are versioned and secret-free
A clean setup reaches the same declared verification results
verification_procedure: Repeat setup in a clean environment and compare command outputs
Inspect lockfiles, tool versions and excluded local state
security_considerations: Verify dependency sources and hashes
Do not bake credentials or private data into images or setup scripts
techniques.fallback_procedure: Record exact tool versions and manual setup steps, and mark environment reproducibility as incomplete.

techniques.name: Continuous Integration
techniques.description: Automatically build and verify every proposed integration with deterministic checks, required status reporting and protected merge gates.
techniques.purpose: Detect integration defects early and make merge readiness depend on current evidence.
techniques.problem_solved: Changes merge without repeatable build, test, schema, security or scope verification.
when_to_use: A shared repository has multiple contributors
Required checks can run deterministically on each change
when_not_to_use: Checks depend on uncontrolled external state
The workflow would require unapproved secrets or paid services
trigger_conditions: A pull request or commit is proposed for integration
A required verification command or schema changes
workflow_steps: Pin the runner and dependency environment
Run syntax, schema, unit, integration and scoped security checks
Publish exact results tied to the commit SHA
Require current passing statuses and independent review before merge
Quarantine flaky checks instead of silently ignoring them
techniques.example_prompt: Review or design CI for this change with deterministic required checks tied to the commit SHA. Block merge on missing or failing evidence and do not claim success from skipped jobs.
techniques.ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: validate future technique data with schema and reference checks before integration without modifying the main registry.
acceptance_criteria: Required checks are deterministic and tied to the exact commit
Missing, failed or stale checks block integration
verification_procedure: Run the CI workflow on a controlled branch and inspect commit-bound results
Test failing and skipped-check fixtures for merge blocking
security_considerations: Protect CI secrets and required statuses
Untrusted PR code must not receive broad credentials or bypass review
techniques.fallback_procedure: Run the declared checks manually on the exact commit and record evidence until CI is available.
